t.1.140.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Knowing that she had been gone a long time, Hiḍimba, the lord of the Rākṣasas, climbed down from that tree and then came toward the Pāṇḍavas.
t.1.140.2: Red-eyed, mighty-armed, with hair standing on end, and of great strength, his body like a mass of clouds, his face blazing with sharp fangs.
t.1.140.3: As soon as she saw him rushing toward them, so hideous in appearance, Hiḍimbā, terrified, spoke these words to Bhīmasena.
t.1.140.4: This wicked-souled man-eater is coming here, enraged. Do as I tell you, together with your brothers.
t.1.140.5: O hero, I can go wherever I wish, and I am endowed with the strength of a rākṣasa. Climb onto these hips of mine, and I will carry you away through the sky.
t.1.140.6: Wake these sleeping ones and your mother, O scorcher of foes; I will take you all and carry you away through the sky.
t.1.140.8: This vilest of Rākṣasas is no match for me, timid one, nor able to withstand my onslaught in battle, nor indeed are all the Rākṣasas together.
t.1.140.7: Do not be afraid, wide-hipped one; he is nothing while I stand here. I shall kill him before your very eyes, slender-waisted one.
t.1.140.9: Look at these well-rounded arms of mine, like the trunks of elephants, my thighs like iron bars, and my broad, compact chest.
t.1.140.10: Today, lovely one, you shall see my prowess, like that of Indra. Do not despise me, broad-hipped lady, thinking me here a mere human.
t.1.140.12: O Bhārata, the enraged man-eating Rākṣasa heard those words of Bhīmasena as he was speaking thus.
t.1.140.11: I do not look down on you, tiger among men, you who have the form of a god; but I have seen the rākṣasa's mighty deeds against men.
t.1.140.13: And Hiḍimba, gazing upon her human form, its hair filled with strings of garlands, its face like the full moon,
t.1.140.15: Seeing her thus bearing a most enchanting human form, and suspecting that she desired a man, the man-eater grew furious.
t.1.140.14: It was a form with lovely brows, nose, eyes and tresses, with very delicate nails and skin, adorned with every ornament and clad in garments of the finest fabric.
t.1.140.17: What evil-minded one is putting an obstacle in my way when I wish to eat? Are you not afraid of my wrath, Hiḍimbā, deluded as you are?
t.1.140.16: Enraged at that sister of his, O best of the Kurus, the Rākṣasa opened wide his large eyes and then spoke these words to her.
t.1.140.18: Shame on you, wanton woman lusting after a man, you who do what is hateful to me, you who bring disgrace upon all the former lords of the Rākṣasas!
t.1.140.19: Clinging to these men, you have done me a very great wrong; I here shall slay them all this very day, and you along with them.
t.1.140.20: Having spoken thus to Hiḍimbā, that red-eyed Hiḍimba rushed at her to kill her, grinding his teeth against his teeth.
t.1.140.21: Seeing him rushing toward him, the splendid Bhīma, best of strikers, rebuked him and said, "Stop! Stop!"
